t: A Buddhist dynasty that ruled Bengal and Bihar for about four centuries, from around 750 to around 1161.
Its kings founded Vikramashila and Somapura and supported Nalanda, the great monastic universities of eastern India.
Pala scholars and art shaped the Buddhism of Tibet, Nepal and Southeast Asia; Atisha left Vikramashila for Tibet.
dyk: Devapala granted five villages to support a monastery at Nalanda built by Balaputradeva, the Shailendra king of Suvarnadvipa (Sumatra), at that king’s request.
ev: Gopala is chosen king of Bengal to end a period of anarchy
Dharmapala installs Chakrayudha as king of Kannauj
Devapala’s Nalanda grant at the request of the Shailendra king Balaputradeva
Mahipala I begins the revival of the Pala kingdom
The Chola king Rajendra I sends an expedition to the Ganges
Ramapala defeats the Kaivarta rebels and recovers Varendra
Death of Madanapala, the last significant Pala king
